item.title: Positive intermediate cohomology of compactified Euclidean space vanishes
item.statement: Assume AC. For $N\ge2$, $0<q<N$, and $R=\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb F_2$, the one-point compactification $(\mathbb R^N)^+\cong S^N$ has $H^q((\mathbb R^N)^+;R)=0$.
item.strategy: Use inverse stereographic projection $x\mapsto(2x/(1+\|x\|^2),(\|x\|^2-1)/(1+\|x\|^2))$, and send infinity to the north pole. This is a homeomorphism: its inverse on the punctured sphere is $y'/(1-y_{N+1})$, and neighborhoods of the north pole correspond to complements of bounded closed sets. The sphere has a CW decomposition with the north pole as its sole zero-cell and the punctured sphere as a single $N$-cell (equivalently $D^N/\partial D^N$). Cellular cochains with constant coefficients have $C^0=R$, $C^N=R$, and $C^q=0$ for $0<q<N$. Hence their degree-$q$ cohomology is zero. Apply the published cellular-cochain theorem. AC is retained from that supplier.

item.title: Finite normal push-off count for an even-dimensional Euclidean immersion
item.statement:
Assume AC. Let $f:M^{2s}\looparrowright\mathbb R^{4s}$, $s\ge1$, be a self-transverse immersion of a closed oriented manifold with no triple points. Orient its orthogonal normal bundle $
u_f$ by $TM\oplus
u_f$ in the standard ambient orientation. Its unordered double points are finite and have ordering-independent signs $\varepsilon(r)$. There exists a transverse smooth section $\sigma$ of $
u_f$, nonzero at all double-point preimages. For every sufficiently small $t>0$, the map $f_t(x)=f(x)+t\sigma(x)$ is transverse to $f$, and $$I(f,f_t)=\langle e(
u_f),[M]angle+2\sum_{r\in\Sigma(f)}\varepsilon(r).$$
item.strategy: This is a direct local adapter, not a citation to a double-point theorem. Finiteness: if ordered coincidences approached the diagonal in compact $M\times M$, their endpoints would eventually lie in a common neighborhood on which $f$ is injective, a contradiction. Thus the off-diagonal coincidence locus is closed in a compact subset away from the diagonal; self-transversality makes it discrete, hence finite. For section existence, take finitely many relatively compact trivializing charts and smooth bumps whose positive interiors cover $M$; extend bump times each frame vector by zero, giving finitely many global sections $s_j$ spanning every normal fiber. The evaluation $(x,b)\mapsto\sum b_js_j(x)$ has surjective vertical differential and is transverse to zero. Parametric transversality gives parameters yielding a transverse section. At the finitely many double-point preimages, zero values impose proper linear subspaces on parameter space; their finite union is null and can be avoided along with the exceptional null set. The zero locus is finite and disjoint from those preimages. For near-diagonal intersections use local normal addition $E(x,v)=f(x)+v$. Its derivative at zero is $(u,w)\mapsto df_xu+w$, an isomorphism. Shrink to finitely many neighborhoods on which $E$ is injective. Then $f(x)=f_t(y)$ with $(x,y)$ sufficiently close to the diagonal means $E(x,0)=E(y,t\sigma(y))$, so $x=y$ and $\sigma(y)=0$. Conversely every zero gives one intersection. At such a point the determinant of the ordered derivative pair is the determinant of $[df,df+t\,d\sigma]$; subtracting the first block from the second gives sign $\det(d^{\rm vert}\sigma)$ in the tangent-first/normal-second orientation. Therefore these contributions sum to the Euler number by the supplied zero-locus theorem. Near each ordered double pair $(x,y)$, the derivative of $G(x',y',t)=f(x')-f(y')-t\sigma(y')$ in $(x',y')$ is invertible at $t=0$. The parameter inverse-function theorem (apply the ordinary theorem to $(G,t)$) gives exactly one nearby intersection for small $t$, of the original ordered branch sign, which is unchanged by continuity of the nonzero determinant. Both ordered pairs contribute $\varepsilon(r)$ because the factor interchange sign is $(-1)^{(2s)^2}=1$. Finally choose disjoint sufficiently small neighborhoods of the diagonal and the finitely many ordered pairs. On their compact complement $\|f(x)-f(y)\|$ has a positive lower bound; boundedness of $\sigma$ excludes any further intersection for small $t$. This also gives transversality globally. No global embedded tube is assumed for the immersed image.

item.title: Top normal classes vanish for Euclidean embeddings
item.statement:
Assume AC. Let $j:M^m\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^{m+k}$ be a smooth embedding of a closed smooth manifold, with $m\ge1$ and $k\ge1$, and let $
u_j$ be its rank-$k$ normal bundle. Then $$ ar w_k(TM)=w_k(
u_j)=0\quad	ext{in }H^k(M;\mathbb F_2).$$ If $
u_j$ is integrally oriented, then also $$e(
u_j)=0\quad	ext{in }H^k(M;\mathbb Z).$$ Together with rank vanishing, $ ar w_i(TM)=0$ for every $i\ge k$. Thus a nonzero top normal class obstructs embedding in codimension $k$, even though rank alone permits that class for an immersion.
item.strategy:
Supply the metric tubular chart of the published collapse definition. Its compact disk tube gives a continuous collapse $c:(\mathbb R^{m+k})^+	o\operatorname{Th}(
u_j)$. The formula at zero vectors says exactly $c\circ j=z$, the Thom-space zero section. For either coefficient ring let $u$ be the corresponding normalized Thom class, regarded as an absolute degree-$k$ class in the Thom space (positive degree). Since $0<k<m+k$, the preceding sphere lemma gives $c^*u=0$. Functoriality gives $z^*u=j^*c^*u=0$. The disk/sphere quotient identification in the inherited Thom interface identifies this pullback with the relative-to-absolute zero-section composite defining $e_R(
u_j)$. For $R=\mathbb F_2$, the published top-Stiefel–Whitney theorem gives $e_2(
u_j)=w_k(
u_j)$; the normal inverse lemma identifies this with $ ar w_k(TM)$. Use $R=\mathbb Z$ for the oriented clause. Compact smooth bases are paracompact and of CW type by the named supplier, so the exact Thom scope holds. AC is inherited from Thom and normal identities. Neither Poincare duality nor an ambient fundamental-class argument is needed; the inherited collapse-PD proposition is compatible but not logically necessary.

item.title: Power-of-two projective spaces do not embed in twice the dimension minus one
item.statement: Assume AC. For every $r\ge1$, put $m=2^r$. Then $\mathbb{RP}^{m}$ does not smoothly embed in $\mathbb R^{2m-1}$. In its mod-two cohomology ring $\mathbb F_2[a]/(a^{m+1})$, $$\bar w(T\mathbb{RP}^m)=(1+a)^{-(m+1)}=1+a+\cdots+a^{m-1},$$ so $\bar w_{m-1}=a^{m-1}\ne0$ contradicts the top-normal-class condition for a rank-$(m-1)$ embedded normal bundle. In particular $\mathbb{RP}^2$ does not embed in $\mathbb R^3$, and $\mathbb{RP}^4$ does not embed in $\mathbb R^7$.
item.strategy: The tangent-class lemma gives $(1+a)^{m+1}$. In characteristic two, $(1+a)^m=1+a^m$ for $m=2^r$. Multiply $(1+a)\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}a^i=1+a^m$, hence $(1+a)^{m+1}\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}a^i=(1+a^m)^2=1+a^{2m}=1$ in the truncated ring. Thus the stated sum is the inverse. Its degree-$m-1$ term is nonzero by the published cohomology-ring example. An embedding into $\mathbb R^{2m-1}$ would have $k=m-1\ge1$ and force that term to vanish by the A-page top-normal-class corollary. No existence of an immersion in $\mathbb R^{2m-1}$, nor embedding in $\mathbb R^{2m}$, is asserted.

item.title: Embedding obstructions include all immersion normal-class obstructions
item.statement:
Assume AC. Every smooth embedding is a smooth immersion ([[def-smooth-embedding]], [[def-immersion-submersion-and-constant-rank-map]]). Hence the normal-class tests of this page also obstruct embeddings: if $M$ is a closed smooth $m$-manifold and $ ar w_i(M)
eq0$ for some $i>k$, then $M$ admits neither an immersion nor an embedding into $\mathbb R^{m+k}$ ([[cor-high-normal-stiefel-whitney-classes-obstruct-low-codimension-immersions]]); if $M$ is connected and $ ar p_i(M)
eq0$ for some $i$ with $2i>k$, then $M$ admits neither an immersion nor an embedding into $\mathbb R^{m+k}$ ([[cor-high-normal-pontryagin-classes-obstruct-oriented-immersions]]). Moreover the normal bundle of an embedding into $\mathbb R^n$ is a genuine rank-$(n-m)$ stable normal inverse ([[lem-an-embedding-into-r-n-gives-the-same-normal-bundle-identity]]), so the rank-vanishing that drives the tests applies to the embedded normal bundle as well. In addition, for $m\ge1$ and $k\ge1$ embedding imposes the stronger condition $ ar w_k(TM)=0$, and an oriented embedded normal bundle must have $e(
u)=0$ ([[cor-top-normal-stiefel-whitney-and-euler-classes-vanish-for-euclidean-embeddings]]). Thus $ ar w_i(TM)
e0$ for any $i\ge k$ obstructs embedding in $\mathbb R^{m+k}$; only $i>k$ is the rank obstruction for immersion. No converse is asserted: these tests are necessary conditions only.
item.strategy: Immediate from the definition of embedding as an injective immersion and the two immersion obstruction corollaries. The embedding case also admits a direct reading: an embedding into $\mathbb R^{m+k}$ has normal bundle of rank $k$, so all normal Stiefel-Whitney classes above degree $k$ and all normal Pontryagin classes with $2i>k$ vanish, which is the same rank-vanishing used for immersions. The last sentence is the boundary recorded again in [[rem-characteristic-class-vanishing-is-only-necessary-for-embedding]]. AC implies the required countable-choice premise by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Retain the two existing rank-test arguments and append the top-class and oriented Euler clauses by [[cor-top-normal-stiefel-whitney-and-euler-classes-vanish-for-euclidean-embeddings]]; distinguish $i\ge k$ for embedding from $i>k$ for immersion.

item.title: Characteristic-class vanishing is only necessary for embedding
item.statement: Assume AC. Remark. For a closed smooth $m$-manifold every embedding into $\mathbb R^n$ has a rank-$(n-m)$ normal bundle, so the vanishing of all normal Stiefel-Whitney classes in degrees $i\ge n-m$ (when $m\ge1$ and $n-m\ge1$), of the Euler class of an oriented embedded normal bundle, and of all normal Pontryagin classes with $2i>n-m$ is necessary for embeddability; the top Stiefel–Whitney and oriented Euler vanishings are embedding-specific here ([[cor-embedding-obstructions-include-all-immersion-normal-class-obstructions]]). It is far from sufficient. Two embeddings can have isomorphic (even trivial) normal bundles and identical stable characteristic classes and still fail to be isotopic: the standard and reflected embeddings of $S^2$ in $\mathbb R^3$ are the elementary example (see the companion page), and in higher codimension knotting phenomena survive every characteristic-class test. The correct additional data are the complement/knotting invariants and the Haefliger-Weber deleted-product (isovariant) classification in the metastable range ([[rem-metastable-embedding-classification-requires-additional-deleted-product-machinery]]), which the present page records only as a boundary and does not build. In particular vanishing of $\bar w$ and $\bar p$ never converts an immersion into an embedding, and Smale-Hirsch theory is not an embedding classification ([[thm-isotopy-extension]] applies only to families of embeddings already given).
item.strategy: Boundary remark, no proof obligation. It records the exact stopping point of the page: the characteristic-class tests are necessary conditions, the even-dimensional Euclidean signed-double-point relation is proved locally, whereas the general Whitney-locus class and knotting/deleted-product invariants are not computed here, and the metastable classification is a sourced non-load-bearing leaf. The elementary witness is worked on the companion page. AC implies the required countable-choice premise by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].

item.title: Normal-class calculation for real projective space
item.statement: Assume AC. In $H^*(\mathbb{RP}^9;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2[a]/(a^{10})$, the normal total class is $$\bar w(\mathbb{RP}^9)=(1+a)^{-10}=\sum_{i\in S_9}a^i=1+a^2+a^4+a^6,$$ because $S_9=\{0,2,4,6\}$: these are exactly the integers $0\le i\le9$ whose binary digits have no overlap with $9=1001_2$. The highest nonzero term is $\bar w_6(\mathbb{RP}^9)=a^6\neq0$, so $\mathbb{RP}^9$ does not immerse in $\mathbb R^{9+k}$ for $k\le5$, i.e. not in $\mathbb R^{14}$, in agreement with the classical computation. For the small case $\mathbb{RP}^4$ one gets $\bar w(\mathbb{RP}^4)=(1+a)^{-5}=1+a+a^2+a^3$, so $\mathbb{RP}^4$ does not immerse in $\mathbb R^5$ or $\mathbb R^6$.
item.strategy: Expand the inverse binomial class by the truncated-polynomial lemma and read off the top nonzero term $a^{d(m)}$; apply the non-immersion theorem. The computation is the standard Milnor-Stasheff illustration for $\mathbb{RP}^m$ and matches MS's $\mathbb{RP}^9$ estimate.

item.title: The Euler class of an oriented even-rank normal bundle controls self-intersection
item.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be an oriented smooth $2m$-manifold and $A^m\subseteq X$ a closed oriented embedded submanifold whose normal bundle $
u_A$ is oriented compatibly, with $m$ even. Then the self-intersection number of [[def-self-intersection-number-of-an-oriented-submanifold]] satisfies $$A\cdot A=\langle e(
u_A),[A]angle,$$ and $e(
u_A)$ is Poincare dual to the zero locus of any smooth section of $
u_A$ transverse to the zero section ([[thm-self-intersection-is-the-euler-number-of-the-normal-bundle]], [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]]). Because the rank $m$ is even, the Euler class is the primary integral invariant of the normal bundle here: for odd rank the Euler class of an oriented bundle is two-torsion ([[prop-euler-class-of-an-oriented-odd-rank-bundle-is-two-torsion]]), so only its mod-two shadow is seen, whereas in even rank the pairing $\langle e(
u_A),[A]angle$ can be a genuine non-torsion obstruction, and $\langle e(
u_A),[A]angle
eq0$ prevents $
u_A$ from admitting a nowhere-zero section ([[prop-a-nowhere-zero-section-forces-the-euler-class-to-vanish]]). Over $\mathbb F_2$, with no orientation hypotheses, the same identities hold with $w_m(
u_A)=e_2(
u_A)$ ([[prop-mod-two-self-intersection-needs-no-orientation]], [[thm-mod-two-euler-class-is-the-top-stiefel-whitney-class]]).

Give $\mathbb R^{2m}$ its standard orientation. Let $M^m$ be a closed oriented smooth manifold with $m$ even, and let $f:M\looparrowright\mathbb R^{2m}$ be a smooth immersion. Its normal bundle $
u_f$, the quotient in [[def-normal-bundle-of-a-formal-immersion]], is oriented by the orientations of $M$ and $\mathbb R^{2m}$. By [[lem-an-immersion-into-r-n-gives-a-rank-n-minus-m-representative-of-the-stable-normal-bundle]], $TM\oplus
u_f\cong\varepsilon^{2m}$. Hence $\langle e(
u_f),[M]angle$ is the signed zero count of any transverse section of $
u_f$; it is invariant under regular homotopy ([[def-regular-homotopy-of-immersions]]) and vanishes if $
u_f$ admits a nowhere-zero section. If $m=2s\ge2$, $f$ is self-transverse and has no triple points, set $D(f)=\sum_{r\in\Sigma(f)}\varepsilon(r)$ with the ordering-independent branch signs. Then $\langle e(
u_f),[M]angle+2D(f)=0.$ In particular the Euler number is even, $D(f)=-\langle e(
u_f),[M]angle/2$, and $\#\Sigma(f) mod2=-\langle e(
u_f),[M]angle/2 mod2$. A nonzero $D(f)$ obstructs regular homotopy to an embedding; in particular odd double-point parity does. No sufficiency criterion or odd-dimensional Whitney identification is asserted.
item.strategy:
The first paragraph is the specialization of the two DT-12 duality theorems to the case where the normal bundle has rank equal to the dimension of the source. The parity clause compares the rank-$m$ case with the published odd-rank Euler-class torsion statement; it records why the integral Euler class is only a mod-two test in odd rank. The push-off/zero-locus dictionary is [[prop-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-oriented-bundle-section-represents-the-euler-dual]]. For the immersion paragraph, let $H:M	imes I	o\mathbb R^{2m}$ be a regular homotopy ([[def-regular-homotopy-of-immersions]]). The vertical derivative is a smooth bundle map $d_MH:\operatorname{pr}_M^*TM	o H^*T\mathbb R^{2m}$ over $M	imes I$ ([[def-vector-bundle-map-over-a-smooth-base-map]]); it is fibrewise injective because every $H_t$ is an immersion. Its image is therefore a rank-$m$ subbundle ([[prop-constant-rank-kernels-and-images-of-bundle-maps-over-one-base-are-subbundles]]), and the quotient is a smooth rank-$m$ vector bundle by [[def-quotient-vector-bundle-by-a-subbundle]] and [[thm-a-vector-bundle-quotient-by-a-subbundle-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]. At each endpoint this quotient is the immersion normal bundle of $H_t$ ([[def-normal-bundle-of-a-formal-immersion]]). Let $j_0,j_1:M	o M	imes I$ be the endpoint inclusions. The orientation of $M$ and the standard orientation of $\mathbb R^{2m}$ induce a continuous orientation on $\mathcal N_H$ through the determinant sequence, whose endpoint orientations are those of $
u_{H_0}$ and $
u_{H_1}$. Naturality of the Euler class ([[thm-naturality-orientation-sign-and-whitney-product-for-euler-classes]]) gives $e(
u_{H_t})=j_t^*e(\mathcal N_H)$ for $t=0,1$, while $j_0$ and $j_1$ are homotopic via $(x,t)\mapsto(x,t)$. Homotopic maps induce the same map in singular cohomology ([[thm-homotopic-maps-induce-equal-maps-in-singular-cohomology]]), so the endpoint Euler classes and hence their evaluations on $[M]$ agree. For the new relation apply [[lem-finite-normal-push-off-count-for-an-even-dimensional-euclidean-immersion]] to get the finite count $I(f,f_t)=e[ M]+2D(f)$. Prove that count is zero without homological intersection imports: the transverse product map $(f,f_t):M	imes M	o\mathbb R^{2m}	imes\mathbb R^{2m}$ intersects the closed oriented diagonal. The determinant calculation of [[thm-intersection-number-under-factor-interchange]], step 1.3, gives $I(f	imes f_t,\Delta)=(-1)^mI(f,f_t)=I(f,f_t)$. Translate the second map by a large constant vector so its image misses the first compact image. This supplies a homotopy to a map missing the diagonal, whose intersection number is zero. [[thm-oriented-intersection-number-is-homotopy-invariant]] therefore gives $I(f,f_t)=0$, proving the equation. The previously supplied normal-bundle-over-$M	imes I$ argument proves invariance of the Euler number under every regular homotopy, even with nongeneric intermediate slices. At an embedding the top-normal-class corollary forces Euler class zero (or repeat its collapse argument); hence nonzero $D$ obstructs such a regular homotopy. Every sign is $1$ modulo two, so parity is $D mod2$. AC implies the required countable-choice premise by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].

item.title: The primary double point obstruction to removing self-intersections
item.statement:
Let $f:M^m\looparrowright X$ be a self-transverse immersion of a closed manifold whose double point set $\Sigma(f)$ is finite; finiteness is part of the hypothesis here (for a self-transverse immersion of a closed $M$ into a $2m$-manifold it holds by [[lem-double-point-locus-has-expected-dimension-two-m-minus-n]] together with compactness). The **primary double point obstruction** of $f$ consists of the following data.
1. **Unoriented part.** The modulo 2 count $\bar I(f):=\#\Sigma(f)\bmod 2\in\mathbb Z_2$. This is defined for every such immersion with no orientation hypothesis.
2. **Oriented part.** If $M$ and $X$ are oriented and $m$ is even, each double point $r$ carries a local sign $\varepsilon(r)\in\{\pm1\}$ independent of the ordering of its two branches ([[def-self-transverse-immersion-and-double-point-locus]]), and the oriented count is
$$I(f):=\sum_{r\in\Sigma(f)}\varepsilon(r)\in\mathbb Z.$$
For $m$ odd the sign of a branch pair changes under interchange of the branches, so only $\bar I(f)$ is intrinsic; equivalently one works with the mod-two count or with a chosen ordering at every double point.
3. **Labelled refinement.** If $X$ is path-connected, every double point $r$ carries a **group label** $g(r)\in\pi_1(X)$ determined by paths in the two branches and a path to the base point; the label is well defined up to conjugation, and for a *pair* $\{r_1,r_2\}$ the Whitney circle formed by the two branches is null-homotopic exactly when the labels agree ([[lem-fundamental-group-label-is-the-obstruction-to-contracting-the-whitney-circle]]). A pair of double points can be removed by the Whitney move only if the labels agree and, with a compatible ordering, the local signs are opposite; when $X$ is simply connected all labels are trivial and the condition reduces to opposite signs.
Necessarily, an embedding has $\Sigma(f)=\varnothing$, so $\bar I(f)=0$ and, when defined, $I(f)=0$. Neither the counts nor their vanishing are asserted to be sufficient for $f$ to be regularly homotopic to an embedding; no general invariance assertion for arbitrary ambient manifolds is needed here, and the count is consumed on this page only through the pairing criterion. In the particular case of an oriented closed even-dimensional $M^m$ immersed self-transversely without triple points in $\mathbb R^{2m}$, the later characteristic-class page proves $2I(f)=-\langle e(\nu_f),[M]\rangle$, so $I(f)$ is invariant under regular homotopy between such endpoints; a connected-sum operation that changes this Euler number cannot be a regular homotopy. The pairing criterion remains ([[prop-whitney-disjunction-removes-algebraically-cancelling-double-points-in-the-stable-range]]).
item.strategy: Definition of the obstruction data attached to a self-transverse immersion: the modulo 2 count, the oriented count where it is intrinsic, and the group-label refinement. Nothing is proved. The well-definedness inputs are the definition of the double point locus ([[def-self-transverse-immersion-and-double-point-locus]]), the local sign conventions of oriented intersection theory ([[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]], [[def-oriented-intersection-number]]), and the label lemma of the Whitney-trick page. The final paragraph records the two caveats honestly: an embedding has empty double point set, but the converse fails, and no general invariance assertion is needed for arbitrary ambient manifolds. In the even-dimensional Euclidean case, the later normal-push-off proof gives twice the signed count as minus the normal Euler number, hence invariance under regular homotopy. An operation changing the normal Euler number by 2 is not a regular homotopy. The definition is used here through the pairwise cancellation criterion, and the remark that follows records that vanishing does not classify embeddings.
